faculty_override_note: The official two-year, four-semester map is the default. The official five-semester map is an alternate lighter-load pathway. DegreeWorks and faculty advisement remain authoritative.
sequence_notes: MAR 100 is a prerequisite for all MAR courses, per the degree maps' own footnote; encoded on each individual MAR course rather than as a single program-wide rule.

MAR 330's official prerequisite is 'ENG 101 and MAT 150 and [MAR 100 or PSY 100]' (quoted exactly from the course-listings page) -- a mixed AND/OR expression. The prerequisite grammar splits on `|` into top-level AND groups first, and each group can independently contain an ` or ` OR-list, so this is fully and exactly expressible as `ENG 101|MAT 150|MAR 100 or PSY 100`.
MAR 220 and MAR 230 both require ENG 101 and MAR 100 (encoded as `ENG 101|MAR 100`); MAR 210 requires only MAR 100.
Program Elective is 9 credits (3 of 7 courses) from MAR 210, MAR 220, MAR 230, BUS 150, CIS 200, COM 245, or MMP 240.

CIS 200's full official prerequisite ('any ACC course or any BUS course, and pass a computer competency test, or CIS 100') is only partially expressible; encoded as `ACC 122 or BUS 104`, matching the identical partial-encoding precedent already established for CIS 200 in bba_as_courses.csv. The computer-competency-test alternative remains an advising check, not enforced.

General Elective is officially 6 credits ('Some of these credits may be satisfied by taking STEM variants in the Common Core'); the two-year map shows only 5 explicit credits (3 + 2 across two semesters) because MAT 150 (4 credits) is one credit above its nominal 3-credit Common Core slot. The data model cannot move credits between groups, so General Elective is modeled as a single flat 6-credit placeholder, matching the pattern already used in eco_aa_courses.csv, crj_aa_courses.csv, and vat_as_courses.csv.
Select any Creative Expression Pathways course other than SPE 100 or SPE 102 for the second Creative Expression requirement.
SPE 102 is modeled as its own row, reciprocally alternate to SPE 100.
A Writing Intensive course is required for graduation.
